questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a type of general insurance?
questions.x: Health Insurance is typically classified under life insurance when it covers long-term or critical illnesses, though it can overlap in some policies.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of a 'Reinsurance' agreement?
o: To sell insurance policies to individuals
To transfer risk from one insurer to another
To invest premiums in the stock market
questions.x: Reinsurance allows insurers to distribute risk by purchasing coverage from other insurers.

questions.q: Which of these is a key principle of insurance?
questions.x: Utmost good faith requires both parties to disclose all relevant information truthfully.

questions.q: What does the term 'Endorsement' refer to in insurance?
o: An amendment to an insurance policy
questions.x: An endorsement modifies the terms of an insurance policy after it has been issued.

questions.q: Which body regulates insurance in India?
questions.x: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) oversees insurance operations.

questions.q: What is the maximum period for which a 'Money-Back' policy typically pays out?
questions.x: Money-back policies usually have a maturity period of 20 years, with partial payouts during the term.

questions.q: What is the role of a 'Proposal Form' in insurance?
o: To collect details for underwriting and policy issuance
questions.x: The proposal form gathers necessary information to assess risk and issue the policy.

questions.q: Which payment system allows **immediate** fund transfers between bank accounts 24x7, including holidays?
questions.x: IMPS (Immediate Payment Service) enables real-time transfers instantly, even on holidays, unlike NEFT (batch-based) or RTGS (limited hours).

questions.q: What is the **minimum amount** that can be transferred via RTGS?
questions.x: RTGS requires a minimum transfer of ₹1,000, unlike NEFT (₹1) or UPI (₹1).

questions.q: Which system uses a **unique identifier** (e.g., MMID + mobile number) for transactions?
questions.x: IMPS uses a **Mobile Money Identifier (MMID)** linked to a mobile number for authentication.

questions.q: UPI transactions are **irreversible** unless initiated within how many hours of the original transaction?
questions.x: UPI allows reversal only if the recipient hasn’t accepted the payment within **1 hour** of the original transaction.

questions.q: RTGS transactions are **settled** in which of the following ways?
questions.x: RTGS uses **real-time gross settlement (RTGS)**, meaning funds are transferred instantly on a **one-to-one** basis.
